drafted_from: tool:list-stripe-events-as-payment-events's own row (its words and input schema) and the take-payments function it runs, whose tests use made-up Stripe replies; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "List my Stripe renewals and refunds since a time as payment events", with {"since_unix": 1793750400, "types": ["invoice.paid", "charge.refunded"], "secret_name": "bakery-stripe-secret-key-test"}. It runs tool:list-stripe-events-as-payment-events and answers {"payment_events": [{"kind": "payment-event", "id": "payment-event:payment:pi_test_sample0201", "event_kind": "subscription.renewed", "occurred_at": "2026-11-04T00:00:00.000Z"}], "next_cursor": null, "complete": true, "cursor_too_old": false, "left_out": 0}.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input, asks Stripe with your own key, and answers; it keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "List my Stripe renewals and refunds since a time as payment events", and give it since_unix and your Stripe key's vault name in secret_name.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:list-stripe-events-as-payment-events and that input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: payment_events to keep once each by its id, and next_cursor to ask for the next page while complete is false.
4. Keep each payment event where you keep your payments, by its id, so the same event kept twice is one row.
